title: Review: Covalent and dative bonding; Lewis structures; Metallic bonding and comparing structures; Giant covalent structures; States of matter and phase changes
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: BD08#t2 term and clue written for the game; BD02#t4 term and clue written for the game; BD06#t2 term and clue written for the game; BD05#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: BD02#N.12b, BD05#N.11a, BD06#N.11, BD08#N.8a, BD02#N.11, BD05#N.7, BD06#N.3a, BD08#N.12, BD02#N.2, BD06#N.13, BD08#N.2a, BD06#N.15. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Deposition
items.clue: Change of state directly from gas to solid.

items.label: Dative bond
items.clue: Formed when one atom supplies both shared electrons, as when H₂O joins H⁺.

items.label: Alloy
items.clue: A mixture such as brass or steel, usually harder and stronger than the pure metal.

items.label: Graphite
items.clue: Flat layers of hexagons that slide over each other, so it is soft, yet it conducts.

questions.stem: Carbon monoxide, CO, has 10 outer electrons, the same as N₂. Like N₂, it has a triple bond and one lone pair on each atom. Which describes the three shared pairs?

options.text: Three ordinary covalent bonds: C and O each supply three electrons.
Two ordinary covalent bonds, plus one co-ordinate bond from C to O.
Three co-ordinate bonds, all from O to C.
Two ordinary covalent bonds, plus one co-ordinate bond from O to C.

questions.explanation: C shares two electrons and O two: two ordinary pairs. O then donates one lone pair to C: C≡O with an arrow O→C. Each atom keeps one lone pair and has 8.

questions.stem: Graphite conducts electricity far better along its layers than at right angles to them. Which statement explains this?

options.text: Its layers slide over each other, and charge is carried only in the direction they slide.
Its ions lie between the layers, so they can move only in the plane of the layers.
Each atom forms four bonds within its layer, so no electrons are left to pass between layers.
Its delocalised electrons move freely within a layer, but cannot easily cross the gap to the next.

questions.explanation: Each C bonds to three others; its fourth electron is delocalised over its own layer only. So charge flows easily along a layer, but hardly between layers.

questions.stem: Four solids, P, Q, R and S, are tested. - P: melts at 801 °C; conducts when molten but not as a solid; dissolves in water. - Q: melts at 1085 °C; conducts as a solid and when molten; insoluble in water. - R: melts at 114 °C; does not conduct as a solid or when molten; insoluble in water. - S: melts at 1710 °C; does not conduct as a solid or when molten; insoluble in water. Which pairing of substance and structure is correct?

options.text: P is metallic, because it conducts when molten.
Q is ionic, because it conducts when molten.
R is molecular, because it melts low and never conducts.
S is ionic, because its melting point is very high.

questions.stem: A molecular solid, X, is heated at a constant rate. Its temperature rises to 80 °C, stays at 80 °C for six minutes while the solid melts, and then rises again. Which explains why the temperature stays constant while X melts?

options.text: The energy supplied is lost to the surroundings, so X absorbs none of it as it melts
The energy absorbed overcomes attractions between molecules; their average Ek is constant
The energy absorbed breaks the covalent bonds within each of the molecules of X
The energy absorbed is used to make each molecule expand as the solid melts

questions.explanation: Temperature measures average kinetic energy. While X melts, the energy separates molecules against their attractions, so the temperature stays constant.

questions.stem: Ammonia, NH₃, reacts with a hydrogen ion, H⁺, to form the ammonium ion, NH₄⁺. Which statement about the bonds in NH₄⁺ is correct?

options.text: The bond formed from the lone pair on nitrogen is longer and weaker than the other three N–H bonds
The new bond formed from a pair of electrons supplied by the H⁺ ion to nitrogen
The new bond formed from one electron supplied by nitrogen and one electron supplied by H⁺
All four N–H bonds are identical, although one formed from the lone pair on nitrogen

questions.explanation: The new bond is co-ordinate: both electrons from N. Once formed, all four N–H bonds have the same length and strength.

questions.stem: Substance X melts at 1710 °C. It does not conduct electricity, either as a solid or when molten. It does not dissolve in water or in hexane. Which structure does X have?

options.text: A lattice of oppositely charged ions
A network of atoms joined by covalent bonds throughout
A lattice of metal cations in a sea of delocalised electrons
Separate small molecules with very strong forces between them

questions.explanation: The very high melting point means strong bonds break. No conduction even when molten means no ions and no delocalised electrons. Insoluble everywhere: a covalent network.

questions.stem: Aluminium is rolled into kitchen foil less than 0.02 mm thick without cracking. Which statement explains this property of aluminium?

options.text: Its layers of cations slide, staying attracted to the delocalised electrons around them.
Its metallic bonds are weak, so the rollers can easily push its atoms apart.
Its bonds between neighbouring atoms bend like hinges instead of breaking.
Its individual atoms are soft, so each one is flattened as it passes between the rollers.

questions.explanation: Metallic bonding is non-directional, so the delocalised electrons keep attracting the cations after the layers have slid. The metal changes shape without cracking.

questions.stem: A drop of steam at 100 °C on the skin causes a far worse burn than a drop of the same mass of water at 100 °C. Which statement explains this?

options.text: Steam molecules at 100 °C have a higher average kinetic energy than water molecules at 100 °C.
Steam releases its enthalpy of vaporisation as it condenses on the skin, then cools like the water.
Steam contains hydrogen and oxygen, which react on the skin and release energy.
Steam is a gas, so each gram of it stores more energy per degree than liquid water does.

questions.explanation: 18 g of steam releases about 41 kJ just by condensing. Cooling 18 g of water from 100 °C to 37 °C releases only about 5 kJ more.

questions.stem: What holds the hydrogen atom and the chlorine atom together in a molecule of hydrogen chloride, HCl?

options.text: The need of each atom to gain a full outer shell by sharing a pair of electrons
The shared pair of electrons itself, acting as a physical link between the atoms
The electrostatic attraction of both nuclei to a shared pair of electrons
The electrostatic attraction between the oppositely charged ions H⁺ and Cl⁻

questions.explanation: The shared pair lies between the H and Cl nuclei and is attracted to both. That attraction is the covalent bond.

questions.stem: Silicon melts at 1414 °C. Phosphorus (white, P₄) melts at 44 °C. Which statement explains the difference?

options.text: Phosphorus has weaker metallic bonding, because its atoms are larger than silicon atoms.
Silicon is giant covalent, so covalent bonds break; phosphorus is P₄ molecules held by weak London forces.
Melting phosphorus breaks its P–P covalent bonds, which are much weaker than Si–Si bonds.
Silicon atoms have more electrons than P₄ molecules, so London forces between them are stronger.

questions.explanation: Melting silicon breaks strong Si–Si covalent bonds throughout the lattice. Melting P₄ overcomes only weak forces between molecules; the P–P bonds stay intact.

questions.stem: Which substance is a compound, and for the correct reason?

options.text: Oxygen, since each of its molecules contains two atoms bonded together
Air, since it contains several elements in the same proportions everywhere
Carbon dioxide, since it contains atoms of two elements bonded in a fixed ratio
Salt water, since the salt and the water have combined to form one new substance

questions.explanation: CO₂ contains carbon and oxygen atoms bonded in a fixed 1 : 2 ratio: a compound.

questions.stem: Each liquid is tested with two electrodes and a bulb. Which liquid will not conduct electricity?

options.text: Molten sodium chloride at 850 °C
Liquid mercury at 20 °C
Liquid titanium(IV) chloride, TiCl₄, at 20 °C
Molten aluminium at 700 °C

questions.explanation: TiCl₄ (boils at 136 °C) is made of small covalent molecules. With no ions and no delocalised electrons, nothing carries charge, even though titanium is a metal.
